Amputation & Prosthetic Rehabilitation

Overview

Life after amputation demands structured physical rehabilitation alongside significant emotional adjustment. Cambridge Hospital supports patients from the early post-operative phase through stump conditioning, prosthetic fitting and training, gait relearning, and adaptive techniques for daily living. Occupational therapists and physiotherapists work together from the first days post-amputation to community reintegration, with home care services continuing support in the patient’s own environment.

Your recovery matters to us, and we are with you every step of the journey.

Care at Cambridge Hospital is a connected journey across inpatient, outpatient, home, and school services, supporting every stage of recovery.

Acquired Brain Injury

Acquired brain injuries, resulting from infection, tumor, hypoxia, or toxic exposure, produce complex, overlapping deficits in movement, cognition, communication, and behavior. Neurorehabilitation assessment guides therapy planning, and family coaching ensures that rehabilitation gains transfer into everyday life across our inpatient, outpatient, and home care services.

Spinal Cord Injury

Overview

Spinal cord injuries, whether complete or incomplete, require long-term, highly coordinated rehabilitation to maximize recovery and prevent secondary complications. At Cambridge Hospital Spinal Cord Injury rehabilitation program supports patients through acute inpatient rehabilitation, progressive mobilization, bowel and bladder management, respiratory physiotherapy, pressure injury prevention, and psychological counselling. Our home care team extends care into the patient’s home environment, enabling safe community reintegration and sustained independence.

Your recovery matters to us, and we are with you every step of the journey.

Parkinson’s Disease

Overview

Parkinson’s disease progressively affects movement, balance, speech, and daily function. While it cannot be cured, the right combination of therapy and medical management can significantly slow its impact. Cambridge Hospital’s rehabilitation services serve Parkinson’s patient by bringing together neurology, physiotherapy, occupational therapy, and speech and language therapy in one coordinated plan, addressing gait, posture, fall prevention, voice, swallowing, and home adaptations. Outpatient and home care options ensure continuity as symptoms evolve.

Your recovery matters to us, and we are with you every step of the journey.

Multiple Sclerosis

Overview

Multiple sclerosis affects the protective coating of nerves in the brain and spinal cord, producing symptoms ranging from fatigue and weakness to problems with vision, balance, and cognition. At Cambridge Hospital, rehabilitation focuses on managing relapses, preserving mobility, building energy-conservation strategies, and supporting emotional well-being. Supervised physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech and swallowing assessment, and psychological support are delivered across inpatient and outpatient settings.

Your recovery matters to us, and we are with you every step of the journey.

Epilepsy

Epilepsy causes recurrent seizures that vary widely in type, severity, and impact on daily life. Families receive seizure-management education, safety planning, and rehabilitation support for any cognitive or physical effects after episodes. For school-aged children, in-school therapy coordination ensures safe, confident participation in the classroom.

Guillain-Barré syndrome

Overview

Guillain-Barré syndrome is a rapid-onset neurological condition causing progressive weakness and paralysis that can require ventilatory support. Recovery is often lengthy and demands intensive, specialist rehabilitation. At Cambridge Hospital, our neuro-rehab team manages GBS patients from the acute recovery phase through ventilator weaning, progressive mobilisation, physiotherapy, occupational therapy, and home care — supporting a full return to function wherever possible.

Your recovery matters to us, and we are with you every step of the journey.

Motor Neuron Diseases

Overview

Motor neuron diseases such as ALS progressively affect the nerves that control movement, breathing, and swallowing. While curative treatment is not yet available, specialist rehabilitation and long-term care significantly improve quality of life and reduces the burden on families. Cambridge Hospital offers a coordinated Motor Neuron Disease therapy and rehabilitation to cover respiratory support, physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech and swallowing care, nutritional management, and psychological support for both patients and caregivers.

Hip Fracture & Femoral Neck Fracture Rehabilitation

Hip fractures, particularly femoral neck fractures, are serious injuries that frequently affect older adults and require prompt, specialist rehabilitation to prevent long-term loss of function and independence. At Cambridge Hospital, our hip fracture rehabilitation begins with safe early mobilization and progresses through weight-bearing exercises, balance retraining, fall-prevention strategies, and occupational therapy for daily living activities. Home Care follow-up is available for patients who need continued support at home.

Fracture Rehabilitation

Overview

Recovering from a fracture requires more than waiting for bone to heal — muscles weaken, joints stiffen, and normal movement patterns are disrupted. Physiotherapy begins as soon as clinically appropriate and is progressed systematically to ensure a safe, full return to function.

Tennis Elbow

Overview

Tennis elbow is a painful condition caused by overuse or repetitive strain of the forearm muscles and tendons, causing pain and tenderness on the outside of the elbow. Despite the name, it affects far more non-athletes than tennis players. At Cambridge Hospital, our outpatient physiotherapy team assesses the underlying biomechanical cause and delivers targeted treatment that includes manual therapy, eccentric strengthening exercises, load management education, and activity modification to ease pain and prevent recurrence.

Your recovery matters to us, and we are with you every step of the journey.

Back Pain & Lumbar Rehabilitation

content.rendered:
Stroke Rehabilitation

Overview

A stroke can change a person’s life in an instant, affecting movement, speech, swallowing, cognition, and emotional well-being. Timely, intensive rehabilitation is the single most important factor in how much function a patient regains. Cambridge Hospital runs a structured post-stroke pathway that begins as soon as a patient is medically stable, progressing through inpatient rehabilitation, outpatient therapy, and home care follow-up. Our programme combines gait and balance training, repetitive task-specific exercises, speech and language therapy, swallowing assessments, and occupational therapy. With family education integrated throughout so that gains made in the clinic carry over into daily life.

Your recovery matters to us, and we are with you every step of the journey.

Care at Cambridge Hospital is a connected journey across inpatient, outpatient, home, and school services, supporting every stage of recovery.
